title: Clean up your Android TV
meta_description: Clean up your Android TV over ADB: drop the ad rows, disable factory apps, replace the home screen. No root needed. Copy-paste prompt and a step-by-step guide.
og_description: Point an AI agent at your TV over ADB, have it disable the apps you never use and replace the home screen. No root, nothing uninstalled, everything reversible.
og_image_alt: Clean up your Android TV - tv.cobanov.dev
promo_text: One more here, and it is free too.
promo_full: A space empire from your terminal
hero_lede: If your TV has gotten sluggish, you can disable the factory apps you never use. Below is a four-step setup and the prompt you hand to an AI agent. Nothing gets uninstalled, every step is reversible. Windows, Mac and Linux all work.

steps.p: On the TV, go to Settings → System → About and press the remote's OK button on the Build row seven times.
Settings → System → Developer options → USB debugging. If there is a separate "Wireless debugging" toggle, turn that on too.
Settings → Network & internet → Status. Note the number starting with 192.168. Your computer has to be on the same network as the TV: same Wi-Fi, or same router.

steps.h3: Open Claude Code or Codex and paste the prompt
steps.p: Copy the text below, replace the two FILL THIS IN placeholders with your TV's model and IP address, and hand it to the agent. It takes care of the rest: installing the tooling, connecting to the TV, doing the cleanup. It checks every change on the TV itself with screenshots, and only stops to ask about what it can't see: sound, the remote, the apps you use.

prompt_credit: The prompt borrows lessons from cleanyourtv, which also keeps ready-made lists for many TV models.

warnings.strong: Never disable a package you can't identify by name
warnings.p: On my TV, disabling com.tcl.suspension killed the "Inputs" button on the remote and I could no longer switch to HDMI. It turned out to be the source-select menu. On some TCL models, com.tcl.providers.config and com.tcl.initsetup drop the Wi-Fi the same way.

warnings.strong: Don't disable the home screen before installing a new one
warnings.p: Install FLauncher and set it as the default first. Only then disable the old launcher. Otherwise you get a black screen.
Unlocking the bootloader factory-resets the TV, and if Widevine drops to L3 Netflix falls back to SD. There is nothing to gain: disable-user already does what root would.

warnings.strong: Turn USB debugging off when you're done
warnings.p: Some TVs cut power to their USB ports while debugging is on. If a USB speaker or drive stops working, switch off USB debugging in Developer options.

undo_p1: Nothing is uninstalled, so every step can be reversed. The agent keeps a list of what it disabled, so telling it "re-enable everything you disabled" is enough.
